subject: Accountancy
notes: Question paper design: remembering and understanding 32 marks, applying 24, analysing, evaluating and creating 24.

chapters.name: Introduction to Accounting
topics: Accounting: concept, meaning, as a source of information, objectives, advantages and limitations
Types of accounting information; users of accounting information and their needs
Qualitative characteristics of accounting information; role of accounting in business
Basic accounting terms: entity, business transaction, capital, drawings, liabilities (non-current and current), assets (non-current and current)
Expenditure (capital and revenue), expense, revenue, income, profit, gain, loss, purchase, sales, goods, stock, debtor, creditor, voucher, discount (trade and cash)
outcomes: Describe the meaning, significance, objectives, advantages and limitations of accounting in the modern economic environment
Identify the individuals and entities that use accounting information for decision making
Explain the terms used in accounting and differentiate related terms like current and non-current, capital and revenue
Give examples of business transactions, liabilities, assets, expenditure and purchases
Explain that sales and purchases include both cash and credit transactions of the accounting year
Differentiate among income, profits and gains

chapters.name: Theory Base of Accounting
topics: Fundamental accounting assumptions; GAAP: concept

Basic accounting concepts: business entity, money measurement, going concern, accounting period, cost concept, dual aspect, revenue recognition, matching, full disclosure, consistency, conservatism, materiality and objectivity
System of accounting; basis of accounting: cash basis and accrual basis
Accounting Standards: applicability of Accounting Standards (AS) and Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)
Goods and Services Tax (GST): characteristics and advantages
outcomes: State the meaning of fundamental accounting assumptions and their relevance in accounting
Describe accounting assumptions and the situations in which each applies during the accounting process
Explain the meaning, applicability, objectives, advantages and limitations of accounting standards
Appreciate that recording of accounting transactions follows the double entry system
Explain the bases of recording transactions and why accrual basis better depicts financial position
Explain the meaning, advantages and characteristics of GST

chapters.name: Recording of Business Transactions
topics: Vouchers and transactions: source documents and vouchers, preparation of vouchers
Accounting equation approach: meaning and analysis; rules of debit and credit
Books of original entry: journal
Special purpose books: simple cash book, cash book with bank column, petty cash book
Purchases book, sales book, purchases return book, sales return book, journal proper
Ledger: format, posting from journal and subsidiary books, balancing of accounts
outcomes: Explain the accounting equation and the effect of a transaction on assets, liabilities, capital, revenue and expenses
Appreciate that vouchers are prepared from source documents for recording transactions
Record transactions in the journal, including simple GST calculation
Prepare different types of cash book and record cash transactions
Record non-cash transactions in the appropriate subsidiary books
Post transactions from subsidiary books and journal proper into ledger accounts
notes: Including trade discount, freight and cartage expenses for simple GST calculation.

chapters.name: Bank Reconciliation Statement
topics: Need for and preparation of bank reconciliation statement
outcomes: Appreciate why the cash book bank balance can differ from the pass book or bank statement
Prepare a bank reconciliation statement

chapters.name: Depreciation, Provisions and Reserves
topics: Depreciation: meaning, features, need, causes, factors; depletion and amortisation
Methods of depreciation: straight line method (SLM) and written down value method (WDV); difference and advantages
Recording depreciation: charging to asset account; creating provision for depreciation / accumulated depreciation account
Treatment of disposal of asset
Provisions and reserves and the difference between them
Types of reserves: revenue, capital, general, specific and secret reserve; difference between capital and revenue reserve
outcomes: Explain the need for depreciation and compute it by different methods
Record depreciation directly in the asset account or through a provision for depreciation account
Record asset disposal through the asset account or an asset disposal account
Appreciate the need for reserves and provisions, and the difference between reserve and reserve fund
notes: Excluding change of method of depreciation.

chapters.name: Trial Balance and Rectification of Errors
topics: Trial balance: objectives, meaning and preparation
Errors: omission, commission, principle and compensating; their effect on trial balance
Detection and rectification of errors that do and do not affect the trial balance
Preparation of suspense account
outcomes: State the need and objectives of a trial balance and prepare one
Understand the types of errors and their effect on the trial balance
Locate and rectify errors and prepare a suspense account
notes: Trial balance with balance method only.

chapters.name: Financial Statements
topics: Meaning, objectives and importance; revenue and capital receipts; revenue and capital expenditure; deferred revenue expenditure
Opening journal entry
Trading and profit and loss account: gross profit, operating profit and net profit
Balance sheet: need, grouping and marshalling of assets and liabilities

Adjustments: closing stock, outstanding and prepaid expenses, accrued income, income received in advance, depreciation, bad debts, provision for doubtful debts, provision for discount on debtors, abnormal loss, goods taken for personal use or staff welfare, interest on capital, manager's commission
Preparation of trading and profit and loss account and balance sheet of a sole proprietorship with adjustments
outcomes: State the meaning and purpose of financial statements
Prepare a trading and profit and loss account showing gross, operating and net profit
Group and marshal assets and liabilities in a balance sheet
Make adjustments for items outside the trial balance and present them in the financial statements

chapters.name: Incomplete Records
topics: Features, reasons and limitations
Ascertainment of profit or loss by statement of affairs method
outcomes: Ascertain profit or loss from incomplete records using the statement of affairs method
